source.title: Inversion dynamics of class manifolds in deep learning reveals tradeoffs underlying generalization
source.authors: Simone Ciceri; Lorenzo Cassani; Matteo Osella; P. Rotondo; Filippo Valle; M. Gherardi

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains networks from random initialization and measures training error during optimization, including at the inversion point. It does not directly report whether training ultimately reaches near-zero error.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that the training error at the inversion point is not special for training-error behavior, and gives the fraction of misclassified training examples there. These intermediate-error results bear on V1 but do not establish the final training-error outcome. Other version topics are absent or not tested. The manifold geometry, pruning, and generalization outcomes are not rows because they do not measure the training-error behavior named by the versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures representation geometry and training error at an intermediate inversion point, not attainment of near-zero training error in the convolutional CIFAR models specified by V1. Its depth, initialization and optimizer comparisons concern inversion dynamics rather than the training outcomes named by V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors find non-monotonic class-manifold segregation associated with a stable set of late-learned examples called stragglers. Inversion-point training error is robust to subsampling and many optimization choices, depends strongly on the dataset and weakly on the tested fully connected architectures. Removing stragglers reduces entanglement and usually worsens clean-test generalization, but can improve performance on sufficiently noisy test data. The authors explicitly qualify robustness in convolutional architectures.
record.recipe_differences: Full-batch gradient descent with cross-entropy on binary-classification tasks; the study examines manifold geometry and stragglers rather than final training-error attainment.
record.method_sensitivity: The inversion dynamics varies with dataset and architecture; unusually large initialization variance can remove the non-monotonicity. CIFAR-10 dynamics are more sharply represented against training error than against epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: At the inversion, approximately 800 of 8192 MNIST examples remain misclassified in a two-layer network with 20 hidden units. This is an intermediate training-error measurement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-manifold segregation reverses at a dataset-dependent intermediate training error.

fits_no_version.finding: The inversion-point error varies little across tested optimizers and initializations; SGD shifts it slightly lower. Excessively large initialization variance can eliminate the geometric inversion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-geometry inversion is robust across many training choices but can disappear at large initialization variance.

record.problems: The paper focuses on internal representations at the first layer, including in deeper architectures. It cautions that the behavior in small fully connected networks may not appear as clearly in state-of-the-art convolutional networks or transformers. It does not report final training-error values relevant to V1.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the explicit training-error observations are intermediate inversion-point measures and do not show whether the networks ultimately attain the endpoint in V1. Figure-only training-error trajectories are not reconstructed as endpoint values.

untested.parts: Near-zero final training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including random labels; the stated smaller-model, early-stopping and regularization qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-related training-error degradation and its prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Loss recovery, curvature evolution and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 classification is unsupported. Intermediate training error does not establish or contradict V1's endpoint claim. No result rows were supplied, and rows_left_out already declares the omitted intermediate measurements and figure-only trajectories.

versions.untested_parts: Whether training ultimately reaches zero or near-zero training error; CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels; smaller models, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious local minima, and extra student width.
Depth effects on training error with and without identity shortcuts; special initialization of deep plain networks; residual networks without normalization.
Whether initialization changes training speed or trainable depth. The paper discusses effects on manifold dynamics, not these outcomes.
Training above stability limits, curvature changes, and edge-of-stability behavior.
Batch normalization’s effect on training speed or tolerated learning rate, and Fixup training without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
